history.summary: NAMING FLAG: the CSV calls this 'Vishnu Temple, Khed' but the shrine is dedicated to Krishna as Ranchhor Rai / Ranchod Ray - documented under its real name. CSV TOWN/DISTRICT FLAG: the temple is at Khed village in BALOTRA district (carved out of Barmer in August 2023), ~8-11 km from Balotra towards Barmer - CSV town 'Barmer' is the old district; documented with the corrected district. COORDINATE FLAG: 25.86306, 72.17222 are the Wikipedia temple-article coordinates; the map geocoder has no temple POI and returns nearby street-level matches (e.g. 25.86367, 72.17142 at Khad Road, Kher) - coordinates are approximate for the site. The Khed Temple (Kher Ranchhoreray Krishna Temple) is a Sanatan pilgrimage site devoted to Krishna as Ranchhor Rai, traditionally said to have been established in the 12th century Vikram Samvat (the Wikipedia infobox's '300 AD' and a local news headline's '1500 years' conflict with this - verify). Khed itself is historically important: it was the early-13th-century capital of the Rathores of western Rajasthan after Rao Sihaji conquered it from the Guhil Rajputs. The temple hosts one of the largest Annakoot fairs in the Jodhpur division on Kartik Purnima, drawing devotees from across India; Janmashtami and Radha Ashtami are also big occasions. name: Vishnu Temple, Khed
town: Khed (CSV town 'Barmer' is imprecise - Khed village, Balotra district, ~8-11 km from Balotra towards Barmer)
town_description: Khed is a historic village on the Balotra-Barmer road in western Rajasthan, once the early-13th-century capital of the Rathores under Rao Sihaji. The Ranchhor Rai temple on the outskirts is the village's main religious landmark, drawing year-round Krishna devotees and large Kartik Purnima crowds.

travel.road: On the Balotra-Barmer road, about 8-11 km from Balotra town (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kartik Purnima (Annakoot Mela) is the biggest occasion.
